assets.alt_text: Three-generation pedigree for Syndrome X. Squares represent males, circles females, and filled symbols affected individuals.
assets.long_description: Generation I: I-1 is an affected female and I-2 an unaffected male; they are connected to the six Generation II individuals. II-1 is an affected male, II-2 an unaffected female, II-3 an affected female, II-4 an unaffected male, II-5 an unaffected male, and II-6 an unaffected female. II-3 and II-4 are connected as a couple, with four Generation III children: III-1 unaffected male, III-2 affected female, III-3 unaffected male, III-4 unaffected female. The legend explains sex and affected status. The question text separately states that II-4 is a known carrier; carrier status is not shaded in this diagram.

assets.alt_text: Three-generation pedigree chart for Syndrome X, showing twelve individuals across generations I, II, and III.
assets.long_description: Standard pedigree notation: squares are males, circles are females, filled symbols are affected. Generation I: I-1, an affected female, is mated to I-2, an unaffected male. Generation II has six individuals: II-1 affected male, II-2 unaffected female, II-3 affected female, II-4 unaffected male, II-5 unaffected male, II-6 unaffected female. II-3 and II-4 are mated. Generation III has their four children: III-1 unaffected, III-2 affected, III-3 unaffected, III-4 unaffected. II-4 is a known carrier.

assets.alt_text: Light-dependent photosynthesis schematic across a thylakoid membrane. Photosystem II, an electron transport chain, photosystem I and ATP synthase are shown. Lumen and stroma are labeled.
assets.long_description: The thylakoid membrane is a vertical band, with lumen on the left and stroma on the right. Light reaches photosystem II and photosystem I. Electron arrows connect photosystem II to the electron transport chain, then to photosystem I and onward to NADP plus on the stroma side, where NADPH is formed. A proton arrow at the electron transport chain runs from stroma to lumen. A proton arrow through ATP synthase runs from lumen to stroma. ADP plus inorganic phosphate and ATP are shown on the stroma side. The diagram is schematic and does not specify molecule counts.

assets.alt_text: Horizontal light-dependent photosynthesis schematic. A thylakoid membrane separates the lumen above from the stroma below; PSII, ETC, PSI, and ATP synthase are shown.
assets.long_description: The thylakoid membrane is a horizontal band, with lumen above and stroma below. PSII means photosystem II, ETC means electron transport chain, and PSI means photosystem I. Light reaches PSII and PSI. Black electron arrows connect PSII to ETC, then to PSI and onward to NADP plus on the stroma side, where NADPH is formed. A blue proton arrow at ETC runs upward from stroma to lumen. A blue proton arrow through ATP synthase runs downward from lumen to stroma. NADP plus with H plus yields NADPH; ADP plus inorganic phosphate yields ATP, both on the stroma side. The diagram is schematic and does not specify molecule counts.
